transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

No matter how interested I am, I can’t keep my attention on job training or applications long enough to finish them. It's incredibly frustrating because I really want to work on cars, but I just can't seem to get through the paperwork or study guides to get my certifications.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated, especially in situations where you need to focus, like during job training or studying?

Yes, I struggle with that a lot. When I'm trying to sit still to study or attend meetings at the job center, my legs are constantly bouncing and my hands are always messing with pens or my keys. I get this pent-up energy in my body, and I feel like I have to get up and pace around just to take the edge off.
Do you often act on impulse, such as blurting out answers before questions have been completed, interrupting others, or intruding on conversations, and if so, can you give me an example?

Yes, I do that a lot, especially during family talks about money or plans. I'll catch myself jumping in before people can even finish their sentences or answering questions that weren't even directed at me. When I realize I've cut them off again, they're always looking really annoyed.

Do you find that your difficulties with attention, such as not being able to finish job applications, are more bothersome to you than your restlessness and impulsive behaviors, or is it the other way around?

The attention and focus issues are definitely more bothersome because they are what's stopping me from keeping a job and finishing my certifications. While the restlessness is annoying, the inability to focus and follow through is what is actually ruining my career plans and keeping me from being financially independent.

Can you estimate how often your impulsivity, such as interrupting others, occurs compared to your inattention, like struggling to finish job applications, and does one clearly happen more frequently than the other in your daily life?

I'm not quite sure which one happens more frequently because both the inattention and the impulsivity feel like constant, daily struggles that disrupt my life in different ways. The trouble with applications and the constant interrupting both happen so often that I've never really tried to compare their frequency. They both just make things really hard for me every single day.

Can you think of any situations where your impulsivity, like interrupting others, happens without you also experiencing significant difficulties with attention or focus, and if so, how often does that occur?

I'm not really sure, as I've never really thought about it that way before. My tendency to jump into conversations and my trouble focusing feel like they're completely tangled up together. I can't really think of any times when one of them happens without the other.

Can you describe a situation where you felt extremely restless or had a strong urge to move, but you were still able to focus and complete a task without interrupting others or making impulsive decisions?

I can't recall a single time where I was feeling that restless but still managed to stay focused and finish what I was doing. Usually, when that pent-up energy hits me, it completely derails my focus. I either have to get up and walk away, or I just end up getting totally distracted and never finish the task.

Do you think your difficulties with restlessness and impulsivity are more prominent and problematic for you in most situations, or is it really the combination of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms that equally affects your daily functioning and causes you distress?

It’s definitely the combination of both that causes me the most distress. While the attention issues and disorganization directly stop me from finishing my applications and certifications, the restlessness and constant need to move make it almost impossible to sit still and actually try to focus in the first place. It really is a double whammy where both sides of it constantly mess up my daily life.

Looking back at your experiences, do you feel that there have been times when either your inattention or your hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms were significantly more severe or prominent than the other, or have they generally been equally problematic for you?

I'm not really sure and I haven't really thought about which one is worse. Both the attention issues and the physical restlessness have been causing me a lot of trouble, and they honestly feel equally hard to handle.

Can you think of any period in your life, such as during childhood or in different living situations, where one set of symptoms, either the inattention or the hyperactivity-impulsivity, was clearly more problematic than the other, and if so, what was different about that time?

I'm not really sure and I haven't ever thought about one being worse than the other. As far as I can remember, both the attention problems and the restlessness have always gone hand-in-hand and caused trouble for me together since childhood. They've just always been mixed together for as long as I can recall.

Are there any specific situations or environments where you feel that one set of symptoms, either your inattention or your hyperactivity and impulsivity, becomes more manageable or less bothersome than the other?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it that way before. Both the attention issues and the restlessness seem to cause me trouble in almost every situation, so I don't think one is ever clearly easier to manage than the other.

When you're in a situation where you can move around freely, like working on cars, do you find that your attention and focus improve, or do you still struggle with completing tasks and following through on your interests?

Even when I'm working hands-on with cars, which I love, I still struggle to stay focused. I'll start a project in the driveway but get sidetracked switching between tasks, or make careless mistakes like swapping numbers on VINs and parts lists when I worked at the garage. Even when I'm just watching engine videos, my mind drifts off, so being interested and moving around still isn't enough to help me focus.

Can you think of any specific times or situations where you were able to manage or overcome your inattention symptoms, but your impulsivity and restlessness still caused significant problems, or vice versa?

I can't really think of a specific time where I successfully managed one of those while the other was still causing problems. For me, the attention issues and the restlessness usually feel completely tangled together and happen at the exact same time. I've just never really experienced them in isolation like that.

Can you recall any instances where you were able to control your impulsivity and restlessness, but still struggled significantly with inattention and disorganization, or has it always been that when one set of symptoms is manageable, the other is as well?

I'm not quite sure because it's really hard to separate the two. I usually feel like both the restlessness and the focus issues are happening at the exact same time, and they are always equally hard to manage.
Can you think of any daily activities or tasks where you are able to control your impulsivity and restlessness without struggling with inattention, such as hobbies or routine chores?

I honestly can't think of any activities or chores where I can successfully control these symptoms. Even with things I really enjoy, like working on cars, or just basic household chores, I still find myself getting distracted, switching between tasks, or feeling constantly restless. It just seems to affect everything I try to do.

Can you estimate how often you experience significant problems with inattention, such as not being able to finish tasks, on days when you do not have significant restlessness or impulsivity, and vice versa?

It's really hard to separate them because I feel like both the attention issues and the restlessness happen pretty much every day together. I don't really have days where I only experience one or the other. They both just seem to affect me at the same time, every single day.
Can you think of any situation where you were able to focus and complete a task without any issues, but still exhibited impulsive behaviors or restlessness, such as interrupting others or fidgeting?

I can't really think of a situation where I could focus perfectly and finish a task without any issues while still being restless or impulsive. Usually, when I am feeling restless, fidgety, or impulsive, my focus is also completely off and I end up getting distracted or leaving the task unfinished.

Can you describe a situation where you experienced significant inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or completing tasks, without also feeling restless or impulsive, and if so, how did you manage to stay focused?

I don't really have a successful way of managing to stay focused, and it's hard to separate the inattention from my restlessness. Even when I try to sit still and focus on a task like a job application, my mind drifts and I quickly start feeling that build-up of restless energy and the urge to move.

Do you think your difficulties with inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity are equally problematic and intertwined in all situations, or are there specific contexts where one set of symptoms clearly dominates over the other?

Actually, different symptoms definitely dominate depending on what I'm trying to do. When I'm doing desk work like filling out job applications, studying, or organizing paperwork, the inattention, getting sidetracked, and feeling overwhelmed are what take over. But when I have to sit still or wait—like in waiting rooms, lines at the bank, or during family discussions—the restlessness, fidgeting, and urge to interrupt completely dominate.

When you're in situations that require a lot of physical activity, like working on cars, do you find that your impulsivity, such as interrupting others, is still a significant problem, or is it more manageable compared to when you're in sedentary situations?

I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about whether my tendency to interrupt people is any different when I'm active versus when I'm sitting still. It's hard to say because it usually just happens without me realizing it in the moment.

Can you think of any situations where you were able to manage your hyperactivity and impulsivity, but still struggled with significant inattention, such as difficulty completing tasks or following instructions, and if so, how did you cope with the inattention in those situations?

I can't really think of a specific time where I successfully managed the physical restlessness while still struggling with my attention. They almost always happen at the same time, and I haven't really found a good way to cope with the inattention in those moments.

Looking back on our conversation, do you think there's a specific pattern or situation where either your inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms clearly overshadow the other, or do they consistently affect you equally?

There is definitely a pattern depending on what I'm trying to do. When I have to do mental tasks like studying, filling out applications, or organizing paperwork, the inattention and focus issues completely take over and block me. But when I'm forced to sit still, wait in lines, or try to relax, the physical restlessness and hyperactivity dominate, so they feel equally disruptive but just strike at different times.

Can you clarify if there are specific times of the day or specific situations where you feel that either your inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms are more pronounced or problematic than the other, and if so, can you describe those situations?

My inattention is most problematic during quiet, focused tasks like filling out job applications, writing up service tickets, or studying my manuals, where my mind constantly drifts and I make careless mistakes. But the restlessness and impulsivity really flare up when I'm forced to sit still or wait, like standing in lines at the bank, sitting through meetings at the job center, or trying not to interrupt during family talks.

Can you estimate the proportion of time in your daily life where inattention symptoms, such as difficulty focusing or completing tasks, dominate over hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms, versus the times when hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms, such as restlessness or interrupting others, are more prominent?

It is really difficult to give an exact proportion or percentage because both types of symptoms feel constantly present and overlap throughout the day. They are so tangled up together that it's hard to separate them or say which one truly dominates my time.

Do you think your difficulties with inattention, such as not being able to finish job applications, are more consistently problematic across different situations and times of the day compared to your hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms?

I'm not really sure and I haven't thought about which one is more consistent throughout the day. Both the attention problems and the physical restlessness cause me a ton of trouble in my daily life, and they both constantly get in the way of me getting back on track.

Considering your daily life and various situations, do you feel that there's a slight leaning towards either inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity being more problematic for you overall, even if both are significant issues?

I’d say the inattention and focus issues feel more destructive right now because they are directly ruining my career and financial independence, like when I forgot my training intake or lost track of paperwork. I am definitely constantly restless and fidgety, but the inability to focus and follow through is what is causing the most immediate crisis in my life.

You've mentioned that both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms are problematic, but if you had to choose, do you think the difficulties with inattention, such as not being able to finish job applications, are slightly more impactful on your daily life than the hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms, or vice versa?

I would definitely say the inattention and organizational difficulties are much more impactful on my daily life. While the physical restlessness is really frustrating, it's the inability to focus, finish applications, and stay organized that is directly preventing me from keeping a job and moving forward in my career. That is what is keeping me financially stuck and unable to live on my own.

Can you summarize which set of symptoms, inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity, you feel has been more consistently problematic for you across different situations and times of the day, considering your overall experience?

Both sets of symptoms are incredibly problematic and constantly feed into each other throughout my day. The inattention, like losing focus and forgetting details, directly ruins my job applications and training, but my constant restlessness and fidgeting make it almost impossible to even sit down and attempt those tasks in the first place. They both feel equally disruptive to my life because they work together to keep me stuck.
Do you think there was ever a period in your life where you experienced significant symptoms of either inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity, but not both, or have they always co-occurred?

As far as I can remember, both the attention issues and the restlessness have always gone hand-in-hand. Even back in elementary school, I struggled with both sides—forgetting my homework and losing track of things, while also blurting out answers and wandering around the classroom. They have just continued to co-occur like that throughout my entire life.
Considering your entire life, do you feel that your difficulties with inattention have generally been more severe or equally severe compared to your hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms?

Looking back, both the inattention and the hyperactivity-impulsivity have felt equally severe and have heavily disrupted my life since childhood. While the inattention and disorganization have severely damaged my ability to keep a job, the physical restlessness and fidgeting have always been there and make trying to focus physically uncomfortable. They really feel like two sides of the same coin, with both severely impacting my daily life.
